messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Sev2 — elevated tail latency for hosted /v1/generate in us-west-2. P95 > 3s, error rate climbing. @leah is on-call.

leah (oncall): ack. seeing the page. starting triage. first ask: customer impact and any obvious mitigations?

sanjay (runtime): quick snapshot from the runtime metrics:
```
queued_requests = 320  # peaked about 10m ago
gpu_pool.available = 0
gpu_pool.total = 48
hpa.desired_replicas = 18
hpa.current_replicas = 12
warmup_latency = 45s  # time between pod provision and ready for inference
inflight_per_gpu = 8
```
Looks like we hit pool saturation and warmups are slow — HPA wanted to scale but pool couldn't hand off GPUs fast enough.

marta (sre): adding some logs from the warmup controller (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T01:12:03Z] warmup-controller: requested node for pod=gen-xyz; status=PROVISIONING
[2026-03-15T01:12:48Z] warmup-controller: node=not-ready; kubelet not registered
[2026-03-15T01:13:20Z] warmup-controller: pod gen-xyz failed readiness check; last error: "nvml init timeout"
[2026-03-15T01:13:50Z] runtime: eviction warning: kv-cache memory pressure
```
Some warmup pods never hit ready state for ~40s, then retry loops add to queue.

owen (infra): cloud provisioning logs show a backlog on attach/format of GPUs in the hypervisor pool — API lag ~22s per instance. We also had a concurrent infra job (nightly reclaim) that was trimming idle nodes; timing was bad. I am suspending reclaim for us-west-2.

leah (oncall): mitigation steps I can push now:
- flip runtime fallback to model-small for hosted tier in us-west-2 (reduces per-request GPU load) :zap:
- enable strict rate-limit for new anonymous customers to flatten surge (throttle window 30s)
- manual scale: bump dedicated warm pool by +6 GPUs (if owens ok)
Please ack and confirm.

sanjay (runtime): ack, i'll trigger fallback toggle (will route 30% traffic to model-small as canary). also pushing a temporary KV cache ttl extension to reduce duplicate compute.

ryan (cust-succ): heard from two paying customers: "response times are slow and one saw 5xxs". Raising incident page to PG for customer comms. We need an ETA to provide to them.

deploy-bot: Automated rollback monitor: no recent deploys to model-serving in the last 12h. No suspicious deploy activity.

marta (sre): building quick timeline:
- 01:10 UTC: traffic surge (bot spike) — queue begins rising
- 01:11 UTC: HPA computes desired=18 based on queued_requests metric
- 01:12 UTC: cloud provider delays GPU attach, warmup latency climb starts
- 01:15 UTC: gpu_pool.available hits 0, queued_requests peaks at 320
- 01:17 UTC: first user-facing 5xxs reported
- 01:20 UTC: mitigations (fallback + throttling) applied, visible p95 improves by 30%
Collecting traces and full controller logs now.

sanjay (runtime): hypothesis thread:
1) primary: warmup provisioning latency + concurrent reclaim job -> transient zero-available GPUs -> HPA stair-step where requests queue faster than pods get ready.
2) secondary: HPA metric (queued_requests) overshoot because it doesn't account for warmup lag, so it asks for more replicas that can't be satisfied because pool==0. This amplifies the queue.
3) possible contributor: KV cache eviction made many cold prefixes hit compute simultaneously.
We should validate with kube events, cloud attach latencies, and kv-cache eviction windows.

owen (infra): confirmed: nightly reclaim triggered 01:08 UTC, reclaimed ~8 idle nodes; reclaim window overlapped with surge. Suspending reclaim prevented further starve. Cloud attach latencies spike chart attached (link) — per-instance attach was 18-25s.

leah (oncall): handoff: @marta please lead the in-incident RCA and own the timeline + hypothesis list. @sanjay please collect kube events and full warmup-controller traces. @owen please keep reclaim suspended and pull provider ticket for attach latency. @ryan collect customer list and impact windows for comms. I'll draft initial postmortem skeleton.

marta (sre): taking it. immediate data we need in-thread for RCA:
- full kube events for gen- pods between 01:05-01:25 UTC
- cloud attach/create logs for nodes provisioned in that window
- HPA metric roll (queued_requests, cpu, custom_gpus_busy) with 10s granularity
- sample request traces (trace ids) for 5xxs
I'll assemble timeline and assign next tasks.

sanjay (runtime): pasted sample kube events (trimmed):
```
01:10:34 Pod gen-abc: pending -> scheduled
01:11:05 Pod gen-abc: scheduled -> container creating
01:11:30 Pod gen-abc: container creating -> waiting for gpu mount
01:12:15 kubelet: device plugin error: NVML timeout
01:12:50 Pod gen-abc: failed readiness
```
This matches the NVML/attach delays marta saw.

ryan (cust-succ): customers impacted list so far: Acme Corp (increased latency 01:12-01:21), BrightApps (saw 5xx at 01:17), internal test harness flagged 30% error rate 01:15-01:18. I'm filing P0 comms for Acme.

leah (oncall): status update: fallback to model-small + throttling live. p95 endpoint down from 3.6s -> 2.2s in dashboards. Error rate trending down. Continue RCA. If we stabilize, we'll move to post-incident notes in 30m.

marta (sre): initial RCA notes in-thread for later PM:
- root cause: insufficient prewarmed capacity + concurrent reclaim job during surge -> GPU pool starvation
- cascade: warmup latency (18-45s) meant HPA/VPA signals overshot queue, leading to user-facing 5xxs
- contributing: kv-cache eviction and metric granularity (10s) delayed HPA reaction bookkeeping

marta (sre): immediate action items (owner):
- [marta] collect and store 01:05-01:25 kube and cloud logs (done: location s3://redwood-incidents/2187654321/)
- [owen] add reclaim guard so reclaim doesn't run if queued_requests > 50 (inflight ticket: INFRA-874)
- [sanjay] make warmup-controller respect a soft prewarm target during business hours (TASK-RUN-120)
- [product] consider exposing a soft quota for hosted to avoid noisy single-tenant bot spikes

leah (oncall): handing off final on-call to @marta for post-incident. I'll be offline for the next 40m but reachable for customer escalations. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

marta (sre): acknowledging handoff. will stitch timeline and invite runtime/infra/product to RCA sync in 2h. Closing in-incident channel, moving details to postmortem doc.

leah (oncall): closing thread here. good work.
